summary.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% to INR 260.55 crore and PAT 73% to INR 60.71 crore, helped by export mix and FX gains.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 260.55 crore (up 22% YoY), PBT INR 82.59 crore (up 70%) and PAT INR 60.71 crore (up 73%). Consolidated revenue was INR 273.35 crore (up 9%), PBT INR 81.23 crore (up 54%) and PAT INR 59.43 crore (up 43%). Management attributed the margin jump to export mix, currency gains, lower freight and other expenses, better operating efficiency and some price pass-through in March. Raw material (paste PVC, yarn) prices rose sharply from early March but supply has normalised and prices have eased somewhat from March highs; automotive price increases are expected to flow through in Q1 FY27 with a 1-2 month lag.

financial_highlights.value: INR 55 crore, including FX gain of about INR 30 crore for the year
INR 290 crore vs INR 194 crore in FY25

segments.name: Export general
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 21 crore; general export market was temporarily hit by Middle East shipment hold and war-related logistics delays.

segments.name: Export OEM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 88 crore; Ford platform volumes increasing after new platforms were added.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 48 crore; price increase taken on domestic open-market footwear customers.

segments.name: PU
segments.commentary: Business described as muted; FY26 revenue about INR 27.08 crore. A large customer approved the company as vendor but no commercial price settlement yet.

guidance_outlook: Export growth guided at 15-20% (value) for the coming years; management said it could reach 20-25% depending on new platforms, with no firm timing.
Domestic growth guided at 8-10% (value), with a similar value growth expected over the next 2-3 years.
Export share of revenue expected at 40-45% in FY27 (value basis), with domestic the balance.
EBITDA margin guided at 25-26% as a base; management said 25-30% is possible in the long term, with 30% dependent on conditions.
Price increases on automotive customers expected to flow through in Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 with a 1-2 month lag; management said full-year margins should even out.

New coating line ordered for an existing India facility (not South India), expected to be commissioned by end of calendar 2026; capacity addition about 5 lakh meters per month, adding about INR 120-150 crore revenue. Management said FY27 cash outflow would be about INR 50 crore.
capex_capacity: New coating line ordered for an existing India facility; completion expected by end of calendar 2026 (plus or minus one month).
Average capacity addition of about 5 lakh meters per month (range 4-6 lakh), implying INR 120-150 crore of revenue.
Global plant (Mexico or other country under evaluation): capex about INR 300 crore; location not yet finalised.
South India plant would have cost about INR 150-200 crore depending on land; the company chose the existing site instead.
US finished goods inventory held at about 8 weeks; transit times lengthened by the war.
demand_pricing: Automotive is the main growth driver in both domestic and export markets; auto OEM exports up about 50% in FY26.
Export prices are fixed in USD for automotive; general export pricing is case-by-case and traders react to currency moves.
Rupee depreciation gave an FX gain (about INR 30 crore for FY26) and improved export competitiveness.
Paste PVC and yarn prices rose sharply from early March 2026 after the war-related petroleum price spike; availability has since normalised.
Q4 FY26 gross margin about 50% and EBITDA margin about 31% (excluding other income), per analyst calculations on the call; management attributed this to export mix, productivity and cost control.

qa_highlights.question: How are paste PVC and yarn prices trending, and is there an availability risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose significantly as a petroleum by-product and softened somewhat from March highs; availability is no longer an issue. Short-term impact is about a month because pass-through lags, while inventory averages it out long term.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 domestic and export growth, and the volume?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 value growth was 15% overall, with exports about 35.5% and domestic about 4%. Volume sold was 31 million meters, up about 4.5-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins rise to about 30%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers cited were the export mix, currency gains, higher operating efficiency, cost control in other expenses and some March price pass-through. Management guided 25-26% as a base and said 25-30% is possible over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: Why was export growth guidance cut from 20%+ to 15-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 15-20% conservative and said export is running above that. Q4 general export was hit by a Middle East hold and US tariff effects, and the company is targeting new customers and platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise from INR 14 crore to INR 17 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a provisional impact of the new labour codes (effective 21 November 2025), booked in Q4 as a catch-up, plus some new hires.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and capacity addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Coating line in an existing India facility, completion by end of calendar 2026, about INR 50 crore in FY27 and about 5 lakh meters per month. Global plant capex about INR 300 crore, location still being evaluated.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (paste PVC, yarn) and the lag in passing on price increases to automotive customers.
Dependence on FX gains; the reported margin uplift includes FX gains, and management did not confirm Q4 margins can be held in Q1 FY27.
Export growth depends on OEM platform ramp-ups (Ford) and on the Middle East and US tariff situation.
Inventory build for the new export business and the 8-week US inventory requirement could weigh on working capital.
Scale and timing of the global plant (about INR 300 crore) remain undecided.
PU business is still muted and no commercial settlement has been reached despite vendor approval.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and margins, but evasive on quarter-to-quarter figures and the sustainability of Q4 margins. Management repeatedly referred to external factors (war, tariffs, raw material prices) and gave ranges rather than firm numbers.
key_quotes: And our volume with Ford was very low. So, we have added more platforms on Ford business.
So, in the long run, yes. If you look at the entire year as a whole, yes, we should be able to do that. I cannot comment on quarter-to-quarter basis right now.
So, we have given a very clear guidance of 25%-26% in the past. We should be able to maintain that for sure.

adds.what: New coating line (~5 lakh meters/month, range 4-6 lakh) at existing India facility, adding INR 120-150 cr revenue
Global plant (Mexico or other country under evaluation), location not finalised

growth.why: Management guides domestic value growth 8-10% and export value growth 15-20% (up to 25% with pipeline) for FY27 and the next 2-3 years, held from prior guidance, backed by a coating line of about 5 lakh meters/month due by end of calendar 2026 and Ford platform additions, though no firm order-book numbers were given for the export pipeline.
